abstract: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is the specialized agency of the United Nations (UN) for information and communication technologies (ICTs). Its primary roles are to allocate global radio-frequency spectrum and satellite orbits, develop the technical standards that ensure networks and technologies seamlessly interconnect, and strive to improve access to ICTs to underserved communities worldwide.

authors.bio: Yukihiro Nishida is an executive research engineer (fellow) with the Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK), Tokyo, Japan. He is the chair of ITU-R SG 6.
authors.name: Yukihiro Nishida

authors.bio: Amir Nafez joined the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), Tehran, Iran, in 1995 and has served as the general director of technical review, supervision, and frequency planning since 2014. He is now a consultant for the organization. He is the chair of ITU-R WP 6A.
authors.name: Amir Nafez

authors.bio: Paul Gardiner is the standards manager with the Advanced Technology Team of European Professional Engineering, Sony Europe B.V. He is a chartered engineer, a member of the U.K. ’s Institution of Engineering and Technology, and a SMPTE Fellow. He is the chair of ITU-R WP 6B.
authors.name: Paul Gardiner

authors.bio: Andy Quested joined the British Broadcasting Corporation as a technical assistant in 1978, becoming a videotape editor in 1985, working on comedy, children’s, and documentary series. He is the chair of ITU-R WP 6C, the cochair of the ITU’s Accessible Media Group and is a SMPTE Fellow.
authors.name: Andy Quested
